problems.title: Compare two fair dice throws
problems.question: A fair die is thrown twice. Find the probability that the first result exceeds the second.
problems.idea: Count ordered pairs.
steps: For second results 1,2,3,4,5,6 there are respectively 5,4,3,2,1,0 larger first results.
The favourable count is 15, so the probability is 15/36.
problems.note: None of the printed choices equals 5/12.

problems.title: Recover the number of white balls
problems.question: A box contains 2 blue balls and some white balls. The probability of drawing white is 0.8. How many white balls are there?
problems.idea: Express the probability as a fraction of the total.

problems.title: Who speaks before both others?
problems.question: Four speakers A,B,C,D speak in random order. Find the probability C speaks before both B and D.
problems.idea: Only the relative order of B,C,D matters.
formulas: Each of B,C,D is equally likely to be first among those three.
steps: There are 3!=6 relative orders. C is first in two: CBD and CDB.
The position of A does not affect this event.

problems.title: A random cut with nearly equal pieces
problems.question: A point is chosen uniformly on a segment of length 10 cm. Find the probability that the two piece lengths differ by at most 2 cm.
problems.idea: Let x be the distance of the cut from one endpoint.

problems.title: A uniformly chosen point in a trapezoid
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD with bases BC=2, AD=3, find the probability a uniformly chosen point lies in triangle ABD.
problems.idea: Use an area ratio.
steps: Divide to get 3/(3+2). The common height cancels.

problems.title: The last positive term of a decreasing progression
problems.question: Find the index of the last positive term of 7.2,6.6,6,… .
problems.idea: Write the general term and impose positivity.
steps: Thus n=12 is the last positive index; a₁₂=0.6 and a₁₃=0.

problems.title: The middle angle of a nine-sided polygon
problems.question: The interior angles of a convex nonagon form an arithmetic progression. Find the fifth angle.
problems.idea: In an odd-length arithmetic progression the middle term equals the average.

problems.title: A right triangle with arithmetic-progression sides
problems.question: The sides of a right triangle form an arithmetic progression. What is its common difference equal to?
problems.idea: Write the sides as t−d,t,t+d.
steps: The Pythagorean equation reduces to t²=4td, giving t=4d.

problems.title: Sum of two-digit multiples
problems.question: Find the sum of all two-digit positive multiples of 7.
problems.idea: They form an arithmetic progression.
steps: The terms run from 14 to 98 with common difference 7.

problems.title: Sum squares of a geometric progression
problems.question: Find the sum of the squares of the first n terms of 2√3,6,… .
problems.idea: The squared terms form another geometric progression.
formulas: Original ratio=√3; squared first term=12; squared ratio=3; S=a(qⁿ−1)/(q−1).

problems.title: Recover a term from consecutive sums
problems.question: A geometric progression has Sₙ=4(2ⁿ−1). Find its fourth term.
problems.idea: A term is the difference of two consecutive partial sums.

problems.title: An infinite alternating geometric sum
problems.question: Solve 1−1/x+1/x²−…=1.5, with |x|>1.
problems.idea: The common ratio is −1/x, whose magnitude is less than 1.

problems.title: Mean versus median of three data values
problems.question: The median of three numbers is 5 above the smallest and 9 below the largest. By how much does the mean exceed the median?
problems.idea: Represent all three numbers using their median m.

problems.title: A dot product after a vector subtraction
problems.question: Find (a−2b)·b for a=(−1,0), b=(−5,1).
problems.idea: First subtract component by component.

problems.title: Two possible collinear division points
problems.question: A=(−2,3), B=(5,−6), and C=(x,y) are collinear with AB:AC=4:3. Which listed value can equal x+y?
problems.idea: A distance ratio permits C in either direction from A.
steps: For t=3/4 the sum is −1/2; for t=−3/4 it is 5/2.
Of the printed choices, only −1/2 appears.
problems.answer: Listed answer −0.5; the other possible sum is 2.5.
problems.note: The ratio alone does not specify whether C lies on ray AB or on its opposite ray. Both sums are possible, though just one is listed.

problems.title: Raise an average by adding one point
problems.question: An applicant has 12 equally weighted subject grades averaging 3.5. In how many subjects must the grade increase by 1 to make the average 4?
problems.idea: Calculate the required increase in total points.
steps: The current total is 12·3.5=42; the target total is 12·4=48.
Each changed subject adds one point, so 48−42=6 subjects are needed.

problems.title: A mode condition determines the ordering
problems.question: The data are 5,0,x,3,x. Their mean equals their median, and the mode exceeds 5. Find x.
problems.idea: The repeated value x must exceed 5.
formulas: For x>5, sorted data are 0,3,5,x,x; median=5.
steps: Then 8+2x=25, so x=8.5, consistent with x>5.

problems.title: Distance between two circle centres
problems.question: Find the distance between the centres of x²+y²−2x+4y=9 and x²+y²−8x−4y=21.
problems.idea: Complete the squares.
steps: The displacement is (3,4), whose length is √(9+16).

problems.title: The greatest squared distance of two vectors
problems.question: Find the maximum of (a−c)²+(b−d)² if a²+b²=1 and c²+d²=9.
problems.idea: The two vectors have lengths 1 and 3.
steps: Their distance is at most 4, so its square is at most 16.
Equality is attained when the vectors point in opposite directions, for example (1,0) and (−3,0).

problems.title: A perpendicular line through an intercept
problems.question: Find the line perpendicular to 2x+y=1 and passing through the x-axis intercept of x−4y=1.
problems.idea: Find the intercept, then use the negative reciprocal slope.
formulas: The given slope is −2; perpendicular slope=1/2.
steps: The second line meets y=0 at (1,0).

problems.title: A point on the y-axis equidistant from two points
problems.question: A point (x,y) on the y-axis is equally distant from (−1,−1) and (2,4). Find x+y.
problems.idea: Set x=0 and equate squared distances.

problems.title: An obtuse angle between parameter vectors
problems.question: Find k such that the angle between (2k,k+2) and (1,k) is obtuse.
problems.idea: The dot product must be negative.
steps: This product is negative between −4 and 0. Both vectors are nonzero there.

problems.title: The acute angle between two lines
problems.question: Find the cosine of the angle between x+y=4 and 3x−y=2.
problems.idea: Use direction vectors and take the absolute dot product for the smaller angle.
steps: The numerator is |1−3|=2; the denominator is √2·√10=2√5.

problems.title: Distance between parallel lines
problems.question: Find the distance between 3x+4y=4 and 3x+4y=−12.
problems.idea: Their left sides have the same normal vector.
steps: The constant difference is 16 and the normal has length 5.

problems.title: The incenter as a weighted vector average
problems.question: In triangle ABC, AB=BC=5, AC=6, and O is the incenter. Express vector OB in terms of m=AB and n=AC.
problems.idea: The incenter is the side-length-weighted average of the vertices.
steps: Take A as the origin, so B=m and C=n. Then O=(6m+5n)/16.
